Given how the rendering system works, it is difficult to completely prevent content from being downloaded once it has been accessed. details:
Summary

I would like to suggest a feature that allows users to control who can see their own avatar based on other users' Trust Ranks.

This setting should control the visibility of the user's avatar to others, rather than which avatars the user can see.

Proposed Features

1. Avatar Visibility Settings by Trust Rank

Allow users to choose which Trust Ranks are permitted to see their avatar.

For example:

Visitor

New User

User

Known User

Trusted User

Users should be able to independently allow or restrict avatar visibility for each Trust Rank.

2. Individual User Visibility Settings

Allow users to set whether their own avatar is visible to specific individuals, regardless of the general Trust Rank settings.

Each individual should have the following options:

Follow the general Trust Rank visibility settings (default).

Always allow this user to see my avatar.

Never allow this user to see my avatar.

This would make it possible to manage exceptions without changing the general settings.

3. Default Settings and First-Time Notification

I suggest allowing all Trust Ranks to see users' avatars by default.

When users first launch VRChat after this feature is introduced, a brief notification should explain the new settings and how to configure them.

Benefits

Helps protect users' avatars from unwanted access by potential bot accounts.

Gives avatar creators greater control over who can see their creations.

Allows users to restrict avatar visibility without unnecessarily excluding legitimate new users.

Provides flexible management through both global Trust Rank settings and individual exceptions.

Conclusion

I believe this feature would improve avatar security and give users greater control over the visibility of their own avatars.

The goal is to provide better protection while maintaining a welcoming and accessible social environment for everyone.

Thank you for considering this suggestion!
title: A proposal for a feature that allows users to control who can see their avatar, based on "trust rank."
